payload.description_as_reported: The sources of information should be both physically and temporally integrated in order to reduce unnecessary search for referents and so reduce extraneous cognitive load.
payload.pattern: Merge the {text_label} and {diagram_element} into a single visual container once the user has spent {dwell_time} seconds on the page, rather than presenting them in separate panels or windows.

provenance.title: The Split-Attention Principle in Multimedia Learning
provenance.quote_or_locus: By eliminating the need to mentally integrate multiple sources of information, extraneous working memory load is reduced, freeing resources for learning

provenance.title: THE SPLIT‐ATTENTION EFFECT AS A FACTOR IN THE DESIGN OF INSTRUCTION
provenance.quote_or_locus: Physical integration (e.g., combining text and diagrams) may reduce cognitive load and so facilitate learning

provenance.title: Principles for Managing Essential Processing in Multimedia Learning: Segmenting, Pre-training, and Modality Principles
provenance.quote_or_locus: The sources of information should be both physically and temporally integrated in order to reduce unnecessary search for referents and so reduce extraneous cognitive load

provenance.title: From Readiness to Response: Assuring Emergency Response Competence Through Scenario-Based Virtual Plant Training
provenance.quote_or_locus: Real incidents, near misses, and process safety requirements were translated into immersive, multi-user control room scenarios that replicate actual control room interfaces, alarm behavior, procedures, communication channels, and operational distractions

provenance.title: Cognitive load and the imagination effect
provenance.quote_or_locus: Imagining a procedure or concept can be a more effective instructional technique than conventional studying, provided the presentation format is integrated rather than split-attention.
